SOS 100

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The drought has devastated farmers in the Karoo, but SOS100 came to the rescue. And since our show aired, the response via donations has been overwhelming - nearly R440,000!

Summary:
We'd go back to where it all started with Adri Williams and interview her at the Khayelitsha Cookies factory.
We would then follow a truck that has tonnes of donations that have been SPECIFICALLY raised from our show (either tuesday/wednesday). The truck is going from Oudtshoorn, but will go to Sutherland - about 4 hours from Cape Town. In Sutherland, (a new part of the Karoo, we did not visit in the last story) we would meet Marinda (a female sheep farmer), who had 600 sheep and now only has 250 sheep. This truck is going to her (and others). We can go with the truck and see the journey and actually be there when there is a donation - see the moment of it arriving and the joy etc. It has yet to rain in Sutherland, which is why I think it's more important we go there rather than Willerston (which is where we went in the first story).

Another nice new twist is that the calls for water for the story all came from WATERSHORTAGE SA- Caroline van Saasen sent 6 trucks of water to them after the story. So that's a nice story intertwined with this update. We would just get the visuals and voice over that part of the update - no need to re-interview her, unless you would like that. Although, she usually prefers for her PR person Ray de Vries to do the interviews - as she lives in Middleburg.

Further information:
Karien from 104fm and her PR manager will give me loads of social media video from the radio station - of people donating - we can see the overwhelming response - I don't think we need to interview them again. I don't think we need to re-interview Pieter Jacobs from the first story, but I will update the audience on his donations. https://www.facebook.com/Tygerberg104FM/ - please see link for some of those visuals


Final figures are still to come later today as to how much they have raised entirely.
So far:
lots of small donations
ABSA - R100,000
Supa Quick - R280,000
Flight Centre - R40,000
1000 bales of hay donated by a farmer in middleburg - and Watershortage SA delivered. And 6 trucks of water went straight to farmers! Just under half a million rand!

There have been a lot of events being hosted - on monday an old age home is hosting a golf day and the entirety of the funds goes to S0S100. Adri said she can send us that footage.

Extra Budget Items:
Flight to Cape Town and car rental - I would need to travel from CT to Sutherland with presenter and we either stay there or drive back. Any other nights I am able to stay with my Parents, and if we use john again, he would stay at his house. So no extra costs there.

I think logistically I would need leave the night before, travel down to Sutherland the day before or day of. Depending on budget.

Script:


In April Carte Blanche visited drought-stricken Willerston in the Karoo.
NATS SOUND
Farmer Pieter Jacobs was praying for rain.
Pieter: “I have been on the farm for 18 years, this is the first time we have had three years of poor rain.”
The rain never came, but Pieter’s prayers were answered by SOS100 – a campaign started by Adri Williams that brought ordinary South Africans to the farmers’ rescue.
Adri: “The project come to light on Christmas day when we had lunch and there I said to my Dad God just dropped it in my heart to fill a truck for farmers and bring it through to them.”
Adri runs nonprofit organization Khayelitsha Cookies, employing 70 women. They donated R17,000 for feed to be delivered to farmers like Pieter. Then, her impassioned pleas for assistance were picked up by Christian Radio station Tygerberg 104FM, who challenged listeners to participate.
Karien “it was the amazing over flowing heart and a grateful spirit that we can just announce … we are at the point of 2.2 Million rand.”
Karien Basson had not, in her 21 years at the radio station, seen support of that magnitude. And, after our story, donations skyrocketed and an additional R500,000 poured in.”
Karien: “Ever since the first TV program of Carte Blanche was aired, about 6-8 weeks ago, we saw incredible balances being paid in, and deposited into our account, Tygerburg 104fm, for project SOS100. We saw amounts of R100,000 and R50,000 from big corporations, believing in this project.”
Karien was moved by a supporter donating her salary.
Karien: “A whole month of salary, she just deposited into our account, saying it’s because I see, what you guys are seeing.”
With the new funds SOS100 looked to find other areas in need – such as Sutherland or Carnarvon, both also in the Karoo. Sutherland’s situation was even worse than Willerston’s. Adri - who is recuperating from a recent car accident - says the phones rang off the hook with offers of aid.
Adri: “And what was Phenomenal, every single truck, as soon as we raised the money, the trucks were loaded and it got delivered, so as to date we’ve helped another 28 farmers.”
Eunice Nyobole who manages Khayelitsha Cookies, says Adri’s campaign to help went from strength to strength.
Eunice: “For me, I didn’t know like South African’s, they wanted to help people but they didn’t know how, it’s like they were waiting for somebody to blow the whistle so they can come, so Adri came out with the way forward.”
Adri: “I can’t explain to you in words, when the farmers received that assistance and that tuck arrived on their farm lands, just how much that meant to them. That was the beacon of hope, that was the beacon of I can carry on.”
Klasie Kersop had tears in his eyes when he saw the trucks loaded with feed.
Klasie: “I thought we were living in a time, when it was each for his own, I didn’t believe there was willingness by other people to help.”
Klassie – who farms sheep - says SOS100 saved his animals from certain death. And then in May - a miracle – the rain returned to Sutherland for the first time in 3 years.
Klasie: “I could taste and smell the rain in the veld, it was an incredible feeling.”
51mm of rain fell - the most seen since 1976.
Karien: “So when the rain came, it was message upon message from farmers, dancing in the rain they just started sending photo’s of literally just streams of living water.”
But the rain brought only temporary relief.
Adri: “They’ve not had the follow up rain, which is also critical, so you can have rainfall, but if you don’t have rainfall within the first two weeks then the crops that start to grow just wither and die.”
Karien: “For the vegetation to restore itself, its going to take, some of the farmers said, up to 6 months, for the vegetation to really restore itself – people mustn’t think for one second that the drought is over, the need is still there.”
Eunice says they’ve seen the need and now the desire to help others has been planted as a seed that SOS100 is helping to multiply.
Eunice: “This world is changing, people are looking at each other, it’s not like before, it’s like okay, we’re all human beings, so if we can all live like that, it’s really what I actually wanted this world, or this country to be.”
